Arthur John Power.title: Arthur Power
Arthur John Power.desc: Royal Navy Admiral of the Fleet (1889–1960)
Arthur John Power.extract: Admiral of the Fleet Sir Arthur John Power (12 April 1889 – 28 January 1960) was a Royal Navy officer. He took part in the First World War as a gunnery officer and saw action in the Dardanelles campaign. Augustus Willington Shelton Agar.title: Augustus Agar
Augustus Willington Shelton Agar.extract: Augustus Willington Shelton Agar, (4 January 1890 – 30 December 1968) was a Royal Navy officer in both the First and the Second World Wars. He was a recipient of the Victoria Cross, the highest award for gallantry in the face of the enemy that can be awarded to British and Commonwealth forces, for sinking a Soviet cruiser during the Russian Civil War. Benjamin Charles Stanley Martin.title: Benjamin Martin (Royal Navy officer)
Benjamin Charles Stanley Martin.extract: Vice-Admiral Sir Benjamin Charles Stanley Martin (18 July 1891 – 3 June 1957) was a Royal Navy officer who was the first boy from the Royal Naval Hospital School, Greenwich, to reach flag rank in the Royal Navy. He was also the first officer from the lower deck to become a rear admiral on the active list in modern times and only the second, after Sir Thomas Spence Lyne, to achieve flag rank at all

Ernst Lindemann.title: Ernst Lindemann
Ernst Lindemann.extract: Otto Ernst Lindemann (28 March 1894 – 27 May 1941) was a German Kapitän zur See (naval captain). He was the only commander of the battleship Bismarck during its eight months of service in World War II. Lindemann joined the German Imperial Navy (German: Kaiserliche Marine) in 1913, and after his basic military training, served on a number of warships during World War I as a wireless telegraphy offi

Eugeniusz Józef Stanisław Pławski.title: Eugeniusz Pławski
Eugeniusz Józef Stanisław Pławski.extract: Eugeniusz Józef Stanisław Pławski (26 March 1895 – 23 May 1972) was a Polish Navy officer who served in World War I and World War II. He was the commander of the ORP Piorun during the hunt for Bismarck.

Helmuth Brinkmann.title: Helmuth Brinkmann
Helmuth Brinkmann.desc: German Admiral and Knight's Cross recipients
Helmuth Brinkmann.extract: Helmuth Brinkmann (12 March 1895 – 26 September 1983) was a Vizeadmiral in the Kriegsmarine during World War II who captained the heavy cruiser Prinz Eugen. Prior to World War II he commanded the aviso Grille, Adolf Hitler's state yacht. He was also a recipient of the Knight's Cross of the Iron Cross of Nazi Germany. Brinkmann surrendered to British troops in 1945 and was held until 1947.

Karl Topp.title: Karl Topp
Karl Topp.extract: Friedrich Karl Topp (29 September 1895 – 24 April 1981) was a naval officer in Germany during both World Wars.

Louis Henry Keppel Hamilton.title: Louis Keppel Hamilton
Louis Henry Keppel Hamilton.extract: Admiral Sir Louis Henry Keppel Hamilton, (31 December 1890 – 27 June 1957) was a Royal Navy admiral. He was Flag Officer in Malta (1943–1945) and later served as First Naval Member and Chief of Naval Staff of the Royal Australian Navy.

Michael Maynard Denny.title: Michael Denny
Michael Maynard Denny.extract: Admiral Sir Michael Maynard Denny, (3 October 1896 – 7 April 1972) was a Royal Navy officer who served as Third Sea Lord from 1949 to 1953.

Philip Louis Vian.title: Philip Vian
Philip Louis Vian.desc: Royal Navy Admiral of the Fleet (1894–1968)
Philip Louis Vian.extract: Admiral of the Fleet Sir Philip Louis Vian, & Two Bars (15 June 1894 – 27 May 1968) was a Royal Navy officer who served in both World Wars. Vian specialised in naval gunnery from the end of the First World War and received several appointments as gunnery officer. Robert St. Vincent Sherbrooke.title: Robert Sherbrooke
Robert St. Vincent Sherbrooke.desc: British officer and recipient of Victoria Cross (1901–1972)
Robert St. Vincent Sherbrooke.extract: Rear-Admiral Robert St Vincent 'Rupert' Sherbrooke, (8 January 1901 – 13 June 1972) was a senior officer in the Royal Navy and a recipient of the Victoria Cross, the highest award for gallantry in the face of the enemy that can be awarded to British and Commonwealth forces.

Richard Taylor White.title: Richard Taylor White
Richard Taylor White.extract: Richard Taylor White (29 January 1908 – 3 March 1995) was a British naval officer in the Second World War. He won three Distinguished Service Orders in the war, all in command of a destroyer.

Wolf Junge.title: Wolf Junge
Wolf Junge.extract: Wolf Junge (5 January 1903 – 21 February 1964) was a German naval officer of World War II. As a Kapitän zur See, he was appointed the executive officer of the battleship Tirpitz in August 1943 under Kapitän zur See Hans Meyer. Edward Lyon Berthon.title: Edward Berthon
Edward Lyon Berthon.extract: Edward Lyon Berthon FRAS (20 February 1813 London – 27 October 1899) was an English inventor and clergyman.

Daniel de Pass.title: Eliot de Pass
Daniel de Pass.extract: Sir Eliot Arthur de Pass (16 March 1851 – 11 July 1937) was an English merchant in the West Indies. He was the founder of EA de Pass & Co., which specialised in trading sugar and coffee from Jamaica.
